# Problem 3: Linear Regression

## Data Preparation and De-identification

```{r youtube-data}
youtube <- read.csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2021/2021-03-02/youtube.csv"
)

# Remove identifiers, descriptive text, and publication information.
remove_columns <- c(
  "brand", "superbowl_ads_dot_com_url", "youtube_url",
  "id", "etag", "published_at", "title",
  "description", "thumbnail", "channel_title"
)

youtube_clean <- youtube[
  , !(names(youtube) %in% remove_columns)
]

data.frame(
  rows = nrow(youtube_clean),
  columns = ncol(youtube_clean)
)
```

## Exploring Potential Outcomes

```{r engagement-summary}
outcomes <- c(
  "view_count", "like_count", "dislike_count",
  "favorite_count", "comment_count"
)

# Summarize each outcome, exclude the missing data
outcome_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(outcomes, function(outcome) {
  x <- youtube_clean[[outcome]]
  observed <- x[!is.na(x)]

  data.frame(
    outcome = outcome,
    missing = sum(is.na(x)),
    unique_values = length(unique(observed)),
    minimum = min(observed),
    median = median(observed),
    mean = mean(observed),
    maximum = max(observed)
  )
}))

print(outcome_summary, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r engagement-distributions, fig.width=10, fig.height=12}
# Plot the original and log-transformed distributions side by side.
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(5, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

invisible(lapply(outcomes, function(outcome) {
  x <- youtube_clean[[outcome]]
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]

  hist(
    x,
    breaks = 25,
    main = outcome,
    xlab = "Original count",
    col = "lightblue"
  )

  hist(
    log1p(x),
    breaks = 25,
    main = paste("log(1 +", outcome, ")"),
    xlab = "Log-transformed count",
    col = "lightgreen"
  )
}))

par(old_par)
```

View counts: Strong right skew and a few extremely large values. Use log(1 + count) 

Like counts: Strong right skew and a few extremely large values. Use log(1 + count)

Dislike counts: Strong right skew and a few extremely large values. Use log(1 + count)

Favorite counts: All observed values are zero, so there is no variation to explain

Comment counts: Strong right skew and a few extremely large values. Use log(1 + count)

```{r transform-engagement}
valid_outcomes <- c(
  "view_count", "like_count", "dislike_count", "comment_count"
)

# Create a log-transformed column for each retained outcome.
log_names <- paste0("log_", valid_outcomes)

youtube_clean[log_names] <- lapply(
  youtube_clean[valid_outcomes],
  log1p
)
```

## Fitting Linear Regression Models

For each outcome and binary characteristic, fit the model

```{r engagement-models}
characteristics <- c(
  "funny", "show_product_quickly", "patriotic",
  "celebrity", "danger", "animals", "use_sex"
)

# Convert logical values to 0 and 1.
youtube_clean[characteristics] <- lapply(
  youtube_clean[characteristics],
  as.integer
)

model_grid <- expand.grid(
  outcome = valid_outcomes,
  characteristic = characteristics,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

model_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  seq_len(nrow(model_grid)),
  function(i) {
    outcome <- model_grid$outcome[i]
    characteristic <- model_grid$characteristic[i]

    # Include one characteristic and continuous year.
    model_formula <- reformulate(
      c(characteristic, "year"),
      response = paste0("log_", outcome)
    )

    # Missing observations are omitted separately for each model.
    fit <- lm(
      model_formula,
      data = youtube_clean,
      na.action = na.omit
    )

    coefficient_table <- summary(fit)$coefficients

    data.frame(
      outcome = outcome,
      characteristic = characteristic,
      estimate = coefficient_table[characteristic, "Estimate"],
      p_value = coefficient_table[characteristic, "Pr(>|t|)"],
      n = nobs(fit)
    )
  }
))

# Identify significant associations at the 0.05 level.
alpha <- 0.05

model_results$significant <- model_results$p_value < alpha
model_results$direction <- ifelse(
  model_results$estimate > 0,
  "positive",
  "negative"
)

# Display all coefficient estimates and p-values.
knitr::kable(model_results, digits = 4)
```

```{r significant-associations}
# Report significant characteristics separately for each outcome.
significance_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  valid_outcomes,
  function(outcome) {
    selected <- subset(
      model_results,
      model_results$outcome == outcome & significant
    )

    associations <- if (nrow(selected) == 0) {
      "None"
    } else {
      paste(
        paste0(
          selected$characteristic,
          " (", selected$direction, ")"
        ),
        collapse = ", "
      )
    }

    data.frame(
      outcome = outcome,
      significant_associations = associations
    )
  }
))

knitr::kable(significance_summary)
```

```{r largest-view-association}
# Extract models for the transformed view count outcome
view_results <- subset(
  model_results,
  outcome == "view_count"
)

# Find the largest positive estimated coefficient
positive_view_results <- subset(view_results, estimate > 0)

largest_positive <- positive_view_results[
  which.max(positive_view_results$estimate),
  c("characteristic", "estimate", "p_value")
]

knitr::kable(largest_positive, digits = 4)
```

None of these characteristics has a statistically significant association with any four of the
outcomes at the 0.05 level.

Danger has the largest positive estimated association. 

## Estimating Regression Coefficients Using Matrix Algebra

```{r select-view-predictor}
# Select the characteristic with the smallest view-count p-value.
best_characteristic <- view_results$characteristic[
  which.min(view_results$p_value)
]

print(best_characteristic)
```

```{r matrix-estimation}
# Use complete observations for the selected model
needed_columns <- c(
  "log_view_count", best_characteristic, "year"
)

model_data <- youtube_clean[
  complete.cases(youtube_clean[, needed_columns]),
  needed_columns
]

# Construct the design matrix:
X <- cbind(
  intercept = 1,
  characteristic = model_data[[best_characteristic]],
  year = model_data$year
)

colnames(X) <- c("(Intercept)", best_characteristic, "year")

# Construct the outcome vector.
Y <- model_data$log_view_count

# Calculate OLS coefficients
beta_matrix <- solve(t(X) %*% X) %*% t(X) %*% Y

print(beta_matrix)
```

```{r compare-matrix-lm}
# Fit the model
comparison_formula <- reformulate(
  c(best_characteristic, "year"),
  response = "log_view_count"
)

fit_lm <- lm(
  comparison_formula,
  data = model_data
)

# Compare the two sets of estimates
comparison <- data.frame(
  term = colnames(X),
  matrix_estimate = as.numeric(beta_matrix),
  lm_estimate = as.numeric(coef(fit_lm)),
  difference = as.numeric(beta_matrix) - as.numeric(coef(fit_lm))
)

knitr::kable(comparison, digits = 8)

# Check agreement within numerical tolerance
all.equal(
  as.numeric(beta_matrix),
  as.numeric(coef(fit_lm)),
  tolerance = 1e-6
)
```
